sentences.t: فَضَحِكَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ أَنْتَ تَأْكُلُ نَشَّالًا وَإِلَّا كَأَنَّكَ طُرْطُورٌ بَدَوِيٌّ تَقَعُ مِنْ بَطْشَةٍ وَإِلَّا أَبُو رِيَاحٍ تَقَعُ مِنَ الْهَوَاءِ وَيْلَكَ يَا مَشْوُمُ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥikat ʿalayhi wa-qālat lahu anta taʾkulu nashshālan wa-illā kaʾannaka ṭurṭūrun badawiyyun taqaʿu min baṭshatin wa-illā abū riyāḥin taqaʿu mina al-hawāʾi waylaka yā mashwumu
sentences.l: And she laughed at him and said to him: You eat a snatcher-way, or else as if you were a Bedouin ṭurṭūr, falling from one blow; or else Abū Riyāḥ falling from the air! Woe to you, O ill-omened one.
sentences.i: She laughed at him and said: Do you eat like a snatcher? Or are you some Bedouin dunce who topples at a single shove, a Father of Winds who falls down from the very air? Woe to you, you creature of ill omen!
sentences.n: This is the girl's mockery and parts of it are obscure. نَشَّالًا is read as an adverbial "snatcher-fashion" (a نَشَّال is a snatcher, pickpocket); the sense is something like "you gobble like a thief", but the passage may be corrupt. طُرْطُور is a tall conical cap and, as an insult, a lanky dunce; the edition marks its first vowel with a ḍamma, which we keep. أَبُو رِيَاح, "Father of Winds", is a nickname for a light, windblown weakling. وَإِلَّا is "or else". The edition marks a ḍamma on the wāw of مشوم, which we keep; the word is مَشْؤُوم mashʾūm, "ill-omened", spelled without its hamza, and it is said as one would say mashūm.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لَهُ اذْهَبْ إِلَى عَسْكَرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَأَرْسِلْ لَنَا غَيْرَكَ لِأَنَّكَ قَلِيلُ الْجُهْدِ وَنَادِ عَلَيْنَا فِى الْعَرَبِ وَالْعَجَمِ وَالتُّرْكِ وَالدَّيْلَمِ كُلُّ مَنْ كَانَ لَهُ قُوَّةٌ يَأْتِي إِلَيْنَا
sentences.tr: thumma qālat lahu idhhab ilā ʿaskari al-muslimīna wa-arsil lanā ghayraka li-annaka qalīlu al-juhdi wa-nādi ʿalaynā fī al-ʿarabi wa-al-ʿajami wa-al-turki wa-al-daylami kullu man kāna lahu quwwatun yaʾtī ilaynā
sentences.l: Then she said to him: Go to the army of the Muslims, and send to us other than you, because you are little of effort; and call upon us among the Arabs and the non-Arabs and the Turks and the Daylamites: every one who has strength, he comes to us.
sentences.i: Then she said to him: Go back to the host of the Muslims and send us someone other than yourself, for you are of small might. And call out for us among the Arabs, the non-Arabs, the Turks and the Daylamites: whoever has strength, let him come to us.
sentences.n: The Daylam are the highlanders of northern Persia, famous as soldiers. كُلُّ مَنْ كَانَ لَهُ قُوَّةٌ يَأْتِي إِلَيْنَا has no particle or lām of command before the verb; the present stands in place of an order, "every one with strength, he comes to us".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَفَزَتْ فَصَارَتْ فِى الْجَانِبِ الْآخَرِ مِنَ النَّهْرِ وَقَالَتْ لِشَرْكَانَ وَهِيَ تَضْحَكُ يَعِزُّ عَلَيَّ فِرَاقُكَ يَا مَوْلَايَ اذْهَبْ إِلَى أَصْحَابِكَ قَبْلَ الصَّبَاحِ لِئَلَّا تَأْتِيَكَ الْبَطَارِقَةُ وَيَأْخُذُونَكَ عَلَى أَسِنَّةِ الرِّمَاحِ وَأَنْتَ مَا فِيكَ قُوَّةٌ لِدَفْعِ النِّسْوَانِ فَكَيْفَ تَدْفَعُ الرِّجَالَ الْفُرْسَانَ
sentences.tr: thumma qafazat fa-ṣārat fī al-jānibi al-ākhari mina al-nahri wa-qālat li-Sharkāna wa-hiya taḍḥaku yaʿizzu ʿalayya firāquka yā mawlāya idhhab ilā aṣḥābika qabla al-ṣabāḥi li-allā taʾtiyaka al-baṭārikatu wa-yaʾkhudhūnaka ʿalā asinnati al-rimāḥi wa-anta mā fīka quwwatun li-dafʿi al-niswāni fa-kayfa tadfaʿu al-rijāla al-fursān
sentences.l: Then she leapt, and became on the other side of the river; and she said to Sharkān, she laughing: It is dear upon me, your parting, O my master! Go to your companions before the morning, lest the patricians come to you and take you on the points of the lances — and you, there is not in you strength for the pushing-away of the women, so how will you push away the men, the horsemen?
sentences.i: Then she leapt across and stood on the farther bank of the river, and said to Sharkān, laughing: It grieves me to part from you, my lord! Go to your companions before morning, lest the patricians come upon you and take you on their spear-points. You have not strength enough to fend off women, so how will you fend off knights?
sentences.n: البَطَارِقَة are the patricians, the Byzantine nobles and commanders. وَيَأْخُذُونَكَ keeps the plural nūn after لِئَلَّا, where Classical would have the subjunctive يَأْخُذُوكَ; the text says it, and we point it so. يَعِزُّ عَلَيَّ is the polite "it is hard on me", but she says it mockingly.

sentences.t: فَتَحَيَّرَ شَرْكَانُ فِي نَفْسِهِ وَقَالَ لَهَا وَقَدْوَلَّتْ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضَةً طَالِبَةً لِلدَّيْرِ يَا سَيِّدَتِي أَتَذْهَبِينَ وَتَتْرُكِينَ الْمُتَيَّمَ الْغَرِيبَ الْمِسْكِينَ الْكَسِيرَ الْقَلْبِ فَالْتَفَتَتْ إِلَيْهِ وَهِيَ تَضْحَكُ ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لَهُ مَا حَاجَتُكَ فَإِنِّي أُجِيبُ دَعْوَتَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-taḥayyara Sharkānu fī nafsihi wa-qāla lahā wa-qadwallat ʿanhu muʿriḍatan ṭālibatan li-al-dayri yā sayyidatī a-tadhhabīna wa-tatrukīna al-mutayyama al-gharība al-miskīna al-kasīra al-qalb fa-iltafatat ilayhi wa-hiya taḍḥaku thumma qālat lahu mā ḥājatuka fa-innī ujību daʿwatak
sentences.l: So Sharkān was bewildered in himself, and said to her — and she had turned away from him, turning-aside, seeking the monastery — O my lady, are you going, and leaving the love-stricken one, the stranger, the poor-one, the broken-one of heart? And she turned to him, she laughing; then she said to him: What is your need? For I answer your call.
sentences.i: Sharkān was bewildered within himself and said to her, when she had turned from him and was making for the monastery: My lady, are you going, and leaving a lover far from home, a poor wretch with a broken heart? She turned back to him, laughing, and said: What do you want? I will answer your call.
sentences.n: وَقَدْوَلَّتْ is printed as one word, wa-qad wallat. The monastery (الدَّيْر) is where the girls live, as the story has set up; it gives the Christian women a place to retreat to. المُتَيَّم is one enthralled by love, "love-stricken". The أَ in أَتَذْهَبِينَ is the question particle "are you…?"; فَإِنِّي …, "for I…", gives her reason for stopping.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ كَيْفَ أَطَأُ أَرْضَكِ وَأَتَحَلَّى بِحَلَاوَةِ لُطْفِكِ وَأَرْجِعُ بِلَا أَكْلِ زَادِكِ وَطَعَامِكِ وَقَدْ صِرْتُ مِنْ بَعْضِ خُدَّامِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla kayfa aṭaʾu arḍaki wa-ataḥallā bi-ḥalāwati luṭfiki wa-arjiʿu bi-lā akli zādiki wa-ṭaʿāmiki wa-qad ṣirtu min baʿḍi khuddāmik
sentences.l: So he said: How shall I tread your land, and sweeten myself with the sweetness of your kindness, and return without the eating of your provision and your food, when I have become of some of your servants?
sentences.i: He said: How can I tread your land, and taste the sweetness of your kindness, and go back without eating of your bread and your provision, when I have become one of your servants?
sentences.n: أَتَحَلَّى بِـ is "to adorn or sweeten oneself with"; the بِـ names the thing used, here the sweetness of her favour. بِلَا is "without", بِـ + لَا. مِنْ بَعْضِ خُدَّامِكِ, "of some of your servants", is the polite "one of your servants". Throughout the speech he is addressing a woman, so the pronouns are feminine (ـكِ).

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَايَأْبَى الْكَرَامَةَ إِلَّالَئِيمٌ تَفَضَّلْ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ عَلَى الرَّأْسِ وَالْعَيْنِ ارْكَبْ جَوَادَكَ وَسِرْ عَلَى جَانِبِ النَّهْرِ مُقَابِلِي فَأَنْتَ فِي ضِيَافَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lāyaʾbā al-karāmata illālaʾīmun tafaḍḍal bi-smi Allāhi ʿalā al-raʾsi wa-al-ʿayni irkab jawādaka wa-sir ʿalā jānibi al-nahri muqābilī fa-anta fī ḍiyāfatī
sentences.l: So she said: None refuses the honour except a base-one. Be gracious — in the name of God — upon the head and the eye. Ride your steed, and go along the side of the river, facing me. So you are in my hospitality.
sentences.i: Then she said: Only a churl refuses hospitality. Be so kind: in God's name, and welcome upon my head and eye. Mount your horse and ride along the river bank, opposite me. For you are my guest.
sentences.n: لَايَأْبَى and إِلَّالَئِيمٌ are each printed as one word (lā yaʾbā, illā laʾīmun). The verb is spelled with a final ى as in the print. عَلَى الرَّأْسِ وَالْعَيْنِ, "on the head and the eye", is the stock phrase of eager welcome: "gladly, and with all honour". تَفَضَّلْ is the polite "please, be so good". ضِيَافَة is guest-right, the protection and entertainment owed to a guest.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ شَرْكَانُ وَبَادَرَ إِلَى جَوَادِهِ وَرَكِبَهُ وَلَازَالَ مَاشِيًا فِي مُقَابِلِهَا وَهِيَ سَائِرَهْ قِبَالَهُ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلَ إِلَى جِسْرٍ مَعْمُولٍ بِأَخْشَابٍ مِنَ الْحَوْرِ وَفِيهِ بُكَرٌ بِسَلَاسِلَ مِنَ الْبُولَادِ وَعَلَيْهَا أَقْفَالٌ فِي كَلَالِيبَ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa Sharkānu wa-bādara ilā jawādihi wa-rakibahu wa-lā zāla māshiyan fī muqābilihā wa-hiya sāʾirah qibālahu ilā an waṣala ilā jisrin maʿmūlin bi-akhshābin mina al-ḥawri wa-fīhi bukarun bi-salāsila mina al-būlādi wa-ʿalayhā aqfālun fī kalālība
sentences.l: And Sharkān rejoiced, and hastened to his steed and mounted it, and did not cease going, in the facing-of-her, while she was going along opposite him, until he reached a bridge made with beams of poplar, and in it pulleys with chains of steel, and upon them locks in hooks.
sentences.i: Sharkān was glad, and hurried to his horse and mounted it, and rode on beside her as she walked along facing him, until he came to a bridge built of poplar beams. It had pulleys hung with steel chains, and on the chains locks fastened in hooks.
sentences.n: The edition spells the feminine ending of سَائِرَة with a final ه; we point it as printed, with a sukūn (sāʾirah), and the same habit recurs. قِبَالَهُ is "opposite him", with the pronoun -hu. مَاشِيًا is "going on, proceeding" even though Sharkān is on horseback. بُكَر, plural of بَكَرَة "pulley", and the chains and hooks suggest a drawbridge that can be raised. بِـ in بِأَخْشَابٍ and بِسَلَاسِلَ marks what the bridge is made or fitted with. بِسَلَاسِلَ and كَلَالِيبَ are diptote plurals, hence the fatḥa where a kasra would be expected.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ شَرْكَانُ إِلَى ذَٰلِكَ الْجِسْرِ وَإِذَا بِالْجَوَارِى اللَّاتِي كُنَّ مَعَهَا فِي الْمُصَارَعَةِ قَائِمَاتٍ يَنْتَظِرْنَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara Sharkānu ilā dhālika al-jisri wa-idhā bi-al-jawārī allātī kunna maʿahā fī al-muṣāraʿati qāʾimātin yantaẓirnahā
sentences.l: And Sharkān looked at that bridge, and behold, with the slave-girls who were with her in the wrestling, standing, awaiting her.
sentences.i: Sharkān looked toward the bridge, and there stood the girls who had been with her at the wrestling, waiting for her.
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِـ is the "suddenly there was" construction: the بِـ only marks what appears, here the girls. The edition writes the final yā' of الْجَوَارِى with ى, as it does in many words; we keep the letter. قَائِمَاتٍ is a circumstantial accusative ("standing"), and يَنْتَظِرْنَهَا has the feminine plural ending -na, so the waiting is by the girls.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيْهِنَّ كَلَّمَتْ جَارِيَةً مِنْهُنَّ بِاسَانِ الرُّومِيَّةِ أَنْ قُومِي إِلَيْهِ وَأَمْسِكِي عِنَانَ جَوَادِهِ وَاعْبُرِي بِهِ إِلَى الدَّيْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aqbalat ʿalayhinna kallamat jāriyatan minhunna bi-lisāni al-Rūmiyyati an qūmī ilayhi wa-amsikī ʿināna jawādihi wa-ʿburī bihi ilā al-dayri
sentences.l: So when she turned-toward them, she spoke to a slave-girl of them in the tongue of the Rūmī, that: Rise to him and hold the rein of his steed and cross with him to the monastery.
sentences.i: When she came up to them she spoke to one of the girls in the Greek tongue: "Go to him, take hold of his horse's rein, and lead him across to the monastery."
sentences.n: The edition prints باسان, which lacks the lām of بِلِسَانِ "in the tongue of"; we point the letters as printed and read the word as bi-lisāni. الرُّومِيَّة is the Byzantine Greek language. أَنْ after a verb of speaking simply introduces what was said, like a colon. أَقْبَلَ عَلَى is "to turn toward, approach", and عَبَرَ بِهِ is "cross with him, take him across", the بِـ making the verb transitive. الدَّيْر is a monastery or convent.

sentences.t: فَسَارَ شَرْكَانُ وَهِيَ قُدَّامَهُ إِلَى أَنْ عَدَّى مِنَ الْجِسْرِ وَقَدِا نْدَهَشَ عَقْلُهُ مِمَّا رَأَى وَقَٰلَ فِي نَفْسِهِ يَا لَيْتَ شِعْرِي لَوْأَنَّ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ كَانَ مَعِي فِي هَذَا الْمَكَانِ وَتَنْظُرُ عَيْنَاهُ إِلَى تِلْكَ الْوُجُوهِ الْحِسَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-sāra Sharkānu wa-hiya quddāmahu ilā an ʿaddā mina al-jisri wa-qadi ndahasha ʿaqluhu mimmā raʾā wa-qāla fī nafsihi yā layta shiʿrī law anna al-wazīra Dandāna kāna maʿī fī hādhā al-makāni wa-tanẓuru ʿaynāhu ilā tilka al-wujūhi al-ḥisān
sentences.l: So Sharkān went, and she before him, until he crossed over from the bridge, and his wit was bewildered by what he saw; and he said in himself: O would that my knowing — if-only-that the vizier Dandān were with me in this place, and his two eyes were looking at those faces, the fair-ones.
sentences.i: Sharkān went on, with her before him, until he had crossed the bridge, and his wits were dazed by what he saw. He said to himself: "If only the vizier Dandān were with me in this place, and could feast his eyes on these fair faces!"
sentences.n: The edition divides وَقَدِا نْدَهَشَ wrongly as وقدا ندهش; it is wa-qad indahasha, "and had been bewildered", and we keep the printed division, pointing the first piece so that it runs into the second. عَدَّى مِنَ الْجِسْرِ is "he crossed over the bridge"; the edition's عدى can also be read ʿadā, with the same sense. The edition prints قل for قال, so it takes the dagger alif (قَٰلَ). يَا لَيْتَ شِعْرِي is normally "would that I knew …" and introduces a question, but here it is only an exclamation leading into لَوْ أَنَّ, "if only"; the edition prints لوان as one word and we leave it fused. After the wish, وَتَنْظُرُ continues in the present: "and his eyes looking".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ الْتَفَتَ إِلَى تِلْكَ الْجَارِيَةِ وَقَالَ لَهَا يَا بَدِيعَةَ الْجَمَالِ الْآنَ قَدْ صَارَ لِي عَلَيْكِ حُرْمَتَانِ حُرْمَةُ الصُّحْبَةِ وَالْأُخْرَى بِسَيْرِي إِى مَنْزِلِكِ وَقَبُولِ ضِيَافَنِكِ وَصِرْتُ تَحْتَ حُكْمِكِ وَزِمَامِكِ
sentences.tr: thumma iltafata ilā tilka al-jāriyati wa-qāla lahā yā badīʿata al-jamāli al-āna qad ṣāra lī ʿalayki ḥurmatāni ḥurmatu al-ṣuḥbati wa-al-ukhrā bi-sayrī ilā manziliki wa-qabūli ḍiyāfatiki wa-ṣirtu taḥta ḥukmiki wa-zimāmiki
sentences.l: Then he turned to that slave-girl and said to her: O wondrous-one of the beauty, now there has come to be to me upon you two inviolable-claims: the claim of companionship, and the other, by my going to your dwelling and the acceptance of your hospitality; and I have become under your judgement and your rein.
sentences.i: Then he turned to the girl and said: "O peerless beauty, I now have two claims upon you: that of our companionship, and that of my coming to your dwelling and accepting your hospitality. I am under your rule and in your keeping."
sentences.n: حُرْمَة is the inviolability that a bond creates, so a companion, and a guest, may claim protection. The edition prints اى where إِلَى "to" is meant, and ضيافنك with a nūn where ضِيَافَتِكِ has a tā'; we point both as printed and read them as ilā and ḍiyāfatiki. Note that الْآنَ is printed with the madda in the edition. بِـ in بِسَيْرِي is "by, through": the second claim arises by his going. زِمَام is the rein or halter, so "in your rein" means in her control.

sentences.t: فَلَوْأَنَّكِ تُنْعِمِينَ عَلَيَّ بِالْمَسِيرِ مَعِي إِلَى بِلَادِ الْإِسْلَامِ وَتَتَفَرَّجِينَ عَلَى كُلِّ سَيِّدٍ ضِرْغَامٍ وَتَعْرِفِينَ مَنْ أَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-law annaki tunʿimīna ʿalayya bi-al-masīri maʿī ilā bilādi al-Islāmi wa-tatafarrajīna ʿalā kulli sayyidin ḍirghāmin wa-taʿrifīna man anā
sentences.l: So if-only-that you would grant-favour upon me with the going with me to the lands of Islam, and look upon every lord, lion, and know who I am.
sentences.i: If only you would do me the kindness of coming with me to the lands of Islam, to behold each lion of a lord there and learn who I am!
sentences.n: فَلَوْ أَنَّكِ, printed as one word فلوانك, is the wish-formula "if only you …", with the verb in the present; the thought is left without a main clause. أَنْعَمَ عَلَيْهِ بِـ is "to favour someone with (something)", so the بِـ introduces the favour: going with him. تَفَرَّجَ عَلَى is "to look on, take in as a spectacle". The edition points عَلَيَّ with its shadda, which we keep. ضِرْغَام "lion" stands beside سَيِّد as an apposition: "lion-lords".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ كَلَامَهُ اغْتَاظَتْ مِنْهُ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ وَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ لَقَدْ كُنْتَ عِنْدِي ذَا عَقْلٍ سَدِيدٍ وَلَٰكِنِّي اطَّلَعْتُ الْآنَ عَلَى مَافِي قَلْبِكَ مِنَ الْفَسَادِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat kalāmahu ightāẓat minhu wa-qālat lahu wa-ḥaqqi al-Masīḥi la-qad kunta ʿindī dhā ʿaqlin sadīdin wa-lākinnī iṭṭalaʿtu al-āna ʿalā māfī qalbika mina al-fasād
sentences.l: So when she heard his speech she was angered at him, and said to him: And by the right of the Messiah, indeed you were with me possessor of a sound mind, but I have now become-informed upon what is in your heart of the corruption.
sentences.i: When she heard what he said she grew angry with him and said: "By the Messiah's right, I took you for a man of sound judgement, but now I have seen the corruption that is in your heart."
sentences.n: وَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ is an oath: the وَ is the oath-particle, "by the right of the Messiah"; she is a Christian, and swears by Christ. عِنْدِي means "in my view". اطَّلَعَ عَلَى is "to come to know, to be made aware of". The edition prints مافي as one word, ما في, "what is in", and we keep it as one. اغْتَاظَ مِنْ is "to be enraged at".

sentences.t: وَكَيْفَ يَجُوزُ لَكَ أَنْ تَتَكَلَّمَ بِكَلِمَةٍ تُنْسَبُ فِيهَا إِلَى الْخِدَاعِ كَيْفَ أَصْنَعُ هَذَا
sentences.tr: wa-kayfa yajūzu laka an tatakallama bi-kalimatin tunsabu fīhā ilā al-khidāʿi kayfa aṣnaʿu hādhā
sentences.l: And how is it allowed to you that you speak with a word in which you are ascribed to deceit? How shall I do this?
sentences.i: And how can it be proper for you to utter a word that brands you with deceit? How could I do such a thing?
sentences.n: The verb تُنْسَبُ can be 2nd person masculine ("you are ascribed") or 3rd person feminine ("it is ascribed", of the word); the sentence is brief and we read it as 2nd person, though "a word in which one is accused of deceit" is close. تَكَلَّمَ بِكَلِمَةٍ is "to speak a word", the بِـ being the verb's own preposition. نَسَبَ إِلَى is "to attribute to". She means that if she went with him, it would be treacherous toward her own people.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا أَعْلَمُ أَنِّي مَتَى حَصَلْتُ عِنْدَ مَلِكِكُمْ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ لَا أَخْلُصُ مِنْهُ لِأَنَّهُ مَافِي صُوَرِهِ وَلَا فِي قُصُورِهِ مِثْلِي
sentences.tr: wa-anā aʿlamu annī matā ḥaṣaltu ʿinda malikikum ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni lā akhluṣu minhu li-annahu māfī ṣuwarihi wa-lā fī quṣūrihi mithlī
sentences.l: And I know that, whenever I come-to-be with your king ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān, I shall not be clear of him, because there is not in his forms, and not in his palaces, the like of me.
sentences.i: For I know that once I am in the hands of your king ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān I shall never get free of him, since among his beauties and in his palaces there is none like me.
sentences.n: The edition prints صوره, which may be ṣuwarihi, "his forms, images", here taken as the fair shapes of his household, or ṣūrihi, "his wall, his city". We read the first, and admit it is a guess; either way it pairs with "his palaces". حَصَلَ عِنْدَ is "to come to be at someone's place". خَلَصَ مِنْ is "to get clear of, escape from". The edition prints مافي as one word.

sentences.t: وَلَوْكَانَ صَاحِبَ بَغْدَادَ وَخُرَاسَانَ الَّذِي لَهُ اثْنَىْ عَشَرَ قَصْرًا فِي كُلِّ قَصْرٍ جَارِيَةٌ عَلَى عَدَدِ أَيَّامِ السَّنَةِ وَالْقُصُورُ عَدَدُ شُهُورِ السَّنَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-law kāna ṣāḥiba Baghdāda wa-Khurāsāna alladhī lahu ithnay ʿashara qaṣran fī kulli qaṣrin jāriyatun ʿalā ʿadadi ayyāmi al-sanati wa-al-quṣūru ʿadadu shuhūri al-sanati
sentences.l: And though he be master of Baghdād and Khurāsān, he who has twelve palaces, in every palace a slave-girl upon the number of the days of the year, and the palaces the number of the months of the year.
sentences.i: Even though he is lord of Baghdād and Khurāsān, who has twelve palaces, as many as the months of the year, and in each palace slave-girls to the number of the days of the year.
sentences.n: ʿUmar is the king of Baghdād and Khurāsān in this tale. The edition prints ولوكان as one word, which we keep. وَلَوْ كَانَ here means "even though he is". The numbers are rhetorical: twelve palaces for the months, and girls to the number of the days, to say that the king's household is vast. The edition spells the number with ى (اثنى), which we point as ithnay, the oblique case. عَدَدُ شُهُورِ السَّنَةِ is a verbless clause: "the palaces are the number of the months".

sentences.t: فَإِنْ حَصَلْتُ عِنْدَهُ مَا فَزِعَ مِنِّي لِأَنَّ اعْتِقَادَكُمْ أَنَّا نَحِلُّ لَكُمْ كَمَا فِي كُتُبِكُمْ حَيْثُ قِيلَ فِيهَا أَوْمَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-in ḥaṣaltu ʿindahu mā faziʿa minnī li-anna iʿtiqādakum annā naḥillu lakum kamā fī kutubikum ḥaythu qīla fīhā aw mā malakat aymānukum
sentences.l: So if I come-to-be with him, he was not frightened from me, because your belief is that we are lawful to you, as in your books, where it was said in them: or what have-possessed your right-hands.
sentences.i: And if I should come to be with him, he would not hold back from me, because your belief is that we are lawful to you, as it stands in your books, where it is said: "or what your right hands possess."
sentences.n: The clause مَا فَزِعَ مِنِّي is obscure. Taken literally it is "he was not frightened of me" (as a result in the main clause of a condition), and the next sentence shows that the sense must be "he will have no scruple about me"; the text may be corrupt, and نَزَعَ "desist" is a candidate. The quotation is the Qurʾānic phrase "or what your right hands possess", meaning slave-girls (see 4:3, 23:6, 70:30). The edition points those words, and we keep its marks, adding only the hamza and the final vowel of أَيْمَانُكُمْ. كَمَا فِي كُتُبِكُمْ: كَـ is "as, like"; she calls the Qurʾān "your books" as a Christian. لِأَنَّ gives the reason.

sentences.t: فَكَيْفَ تُكَلِّمُنِي بِهَذَا الْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-kayfa tukallimunī bi-hādhā al-kalāmi
sentences.l: So how do you speak to me with this speech?
sentences.i: How, then, can you speak to me in such a way?
sentences.n: كَلَّمَ بِـ is "to speak to (someone) with (words)"; the بِـ gives the means, here the words he used. The فَـ makes the question follow from what she has just said.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا قَوْلُكَ وَتَتَفَرَّجِينَ عَلَى شُجْعَانِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَوَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ إِنَّكَ قُلْتَ قَوْلًا غَيْرَ صَحِيحٍ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā qawluka wa-tatafarrajīna ʿalā shujʿāni al-muslimīna fa-wa-ḥaqqi al-Masīḥi innaka qulta qawlan ghayra ṣaḥīḥin
sentences.l: And as for your saying "and you will look upon the brave-ones of the Muslims" — then by the right of the Messiah, you have said a saying not sound.
sentences.i: As for your saying that I should look upon the Muslim heroes: by the Messiah's right, that was an unsound thing to say.
sentences.n: وَأَمَّا … فَـ is "as for … then …": the فَـ before the oath opens the main clause. The words وَتَتَفَرَّجِينَ عَلَى شُجْعَانِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ are quoted from Sharkān's speech, so the verb keeps its feminine ending. شُجْعَان is the plural of شُجَاع, "brave". غَيْرَ صَحِيحٍ "not sound" is the mild way of saying "false" or "wrong".

sentences.t: فَإِنِّي رَأَيْتُ عَسْكَرَكُمْ لَمَّا اسْتَقْبَلْتُمْ أَرْضَنَا وَبِلَادَنَا مُنْذُ هَذَيْنِ الْيَوْمَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-innī raʾaytu ʿaskarakum lammā istaqbaltum arḍanā wa-bilādanā mundhu hadhayni al-yawmayn
sentences.l: For I saw your army when you faced our earth and our lands, since these two days.
sentences.i: For I have watched your host since you came upon our earth and our lands these two days past.
sentences.n: The speaker is the girl, answering Sharkān, who has been boasting. استقبل is "to face, advance toward", here "to approach"; مُنْذُ هَذَيْنِ الْيَوْمَيْنِ is "since these two days", that is, for the last two days. The edition prints رأيت with a precomposed hamza; the print's own character is kept.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَقْبَلْتُمْ لَمْ أَرَ تَرْبِيَتَكُمْ تَرْبِيَةَ مُلُوكٍ وَإِنَّمَا رَأَيْتُكُمْ طَوَائِفَ مُجْتَمِعِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aqbaltum lam ara tarbiyatakum tarbiyata mulūkin wa-innamā raʾaytukum ṭawāʾifa mujtamiʿīn
sentences.l: And when you came on, I did not see your upbringing an upbringing of kings, and only I saw you bands gathered-ones.
sentences.i: And when you came on, I saw in your rearing no kingly rearing; I saw only bands of men gathered together.
sentences.n: لَمْ أَرَ is the jussive of رَأَى, "to see", with the final vowel dropped; it takes two objects, "your training (as) the training of kings". طَوَائِف, "bands, parties", is a diptote and so takes only a fatḥa; it is the second object of رَأَيْتُكُمْ, "I saw you (as) bands".

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا قَوْلُكَ تَعْرِفِينَ مَنْ أَنَا فَأَنَا لَا أَصْنَعُ مَعَكَ جَمِيلًا لِأَجْلِ إِجْلَا لَكَ وَإِنَّمَا أَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ لِأَجْلِ الْفَخْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā qawluka taʿrifīna man anā fa-anā lā aṣnaʿu maʿaka jamīlan li-ajli ijlā laka wa-innamā afʿalu dhālika li-ajli al-fakhr
sentences.l: And as for your saying "do you know who I am": I do not make with you a fair-thing for the sake of honouring-of to you, and I only do that for the sake of pride.
sentences.i: As for your asking "Do you know who I am?" — I do you no kindness out of reverence for you; I do this only for the sake of pride.
sentences.n: The edition splits إجلالك, "your honouring", into اجلا لك. We keep the printed division and point it إِجْلَا لَكَ, which reads together as ijlālaka. قَوْلُكَ is "your saying", the words he addressed to her as a woman (تَعْرِفِينَ is feminine). صَنَعَ مَعَ … جَمِيلًا is "to do a good turn to someone". لِأَجْلِ is "for the sake of".

sentences.t: وَمِثْلُكَ لَا يَقُولُ لِمِثْلِي ذَلِكَ وَلَوْ كُنْتَ شَرْكَانَ ابْنَ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ الَّذِي ظَهَرَ فِي هَذَا الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-mithluka lā yaqūlu li-mithlī dhālika wa-law kunta Sharkāna ibna al-maliki ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni alladhī ẓahara fī hādhā al-zamān
sentences.l: And one-like you does not say to one-like me that, even if you were Sharkān son of the king ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān, who appeared in this time.
sentences.i: A man like you does not say that to a woman like me — not even if you were Sharkān, son of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, the prince who has risen in this age.
sentences.n: مِثْلُكَ and مِثْلِي, "one like you", "one like me", is a courteous and a proud way of saying "you" and "I". After لَوْ the predicate شَرْكَانَ is accusative, as after any كَانَ. In ابْنَ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ the first ابْنَ is accusative as an apposition to شَرْكَانَ; the second, in عُمَرَ بْنِ, is the printed بن without an alif, as usual between two names.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا وَأَنْتِ تَعْرِفِينَ شَرْكَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā wa-anti taʿrifīna Sharkāna
sentences.l: So I said to her: And you, you know Sharkān?
sentences.i: Then I said to her, "And do you know Sharkān?"
sentences.n: A surprise: the verb is first person, "I said", and the edition even marks the ت with a damma (kept in the pointing). Everywhere else in this passage the story is told about Sharkān in the third person, as in the next unit. We keep what is printed; it may be a slip for فَقَالَ, or Sharkān's own voice breaking in.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ نَعَمْ وَعَرَفْتُ قُدُومَهُ مَعَ الْعَسَاكِرِ وَعِدَّتُهُمْ عَشَرَةُ آلَافِ فَارِسٍ وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ وَالِدَهُ عُمَرَ بْنَ النُّعْمَانِ أَرْسَلَ مَعَهُ هَذَا الْجَيْشَ لِنُصْرَةِ مَلِكِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: qālat naʿam wa-ʿaraftu qudūmahu maʿa al-ʿasākiri wa-ʿiddatuhum ʿasharatu ālāfi fārisin wa-dhālika anna wālidahu ʿUmara ibna al-Nuʿmāni arsala maʿahu hādhā al-jaysha li-nuṣrati maliki al-Qusṭanṭīniyya
sentences.l: She said: Yes, and I knew his coming with the armies, and their number ten thousand horsemen; and that is that his father ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān sent with him this army for the helping-of the king of Constantinople.
sentences.i: She said: "Yes. I knew of his coming with the armies, ten thousand horsemen in all; his father ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān sent this host with him to aid the king of Constantinople."
sentences.n: عَرَفْتُ قُدُومَهُ is "I knew of his arrival". عِدَّة is the count or equipment of a force; here "their number". لِنُصْرَةِ is the لِـ of purpose, "for the helping of".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شَرْكَانُ يَاسَيِّدَتِي أَقْسَمْتُ عَلَيْكِ بِمَا تَعْتَقِدِينَ مِنْ دِينِكِ حَدِّثِينِي عَنْ سَبَبِ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى يَظْهَرَ لِي الصِّدْقُ مِنَ الْكَذِبِ وَمَنْ يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ وَبَالُ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Sharkānu yāsayyidatī aqsamtu ʿalayki bi-mā taʿtaqidīna min dīniki ḥaddithīnī ʿan sababi dhālika ḥattā yaẓhara lī al-ṣidqu mina al-kadhibi wa-man yakūnu ʿalayhi wabālu dhālika
sentences.l: So Sharkān said: O my lady, I have sworn upon you by what you hold-as-creed of your religion, tell me about the cause of that, until the truth appears to me from the lie, and who it is upon whom is the ill-consequence of that.
sentences.i: Then Sharkān said: "My lady, I adjure you by what you hold sacred in your religion: tell me the cause of this, that I may tell truth from falsehood, and see on whom the blame for it falls."
sentences.n: The edition prints ياسيدتي as one word, yā + sayyidatī; it is kept so. أَقْسَمْتُ عَلَيْكِ بِـ is "I adjure you by": عَلَى is the person adjured, بِـ the thing sworn by. حَتَّى + the subjunctive (يَظْهَرَ) gives "so that … may appear". وَبَال, "ill-consequence, guilt", is the burden that falls on the one at fault.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ وَحَقِّ دِينِكَ لَوْلَا أَنِّي خِفْتُ أَنْ يَشِيعَ خَبَرِي أَنِّي مِنْ بَنَاتِ الرُّومِ لَكُنْتُ خَاطَرْتُ بِنَفْسِي وَبَارَزْتُ عَشَرَةَ آلَافِ فَارِسٍ وَقَتَلْتُ مُقَدَّمَهُمُ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ وَظَفِرْتُ بِفَارِسِ سَهْمِ شَرْكَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu wa-ḥaqqi dīnika lawlā annī khiftu an yashīʿa khabarī annī min banāti al-Rūmi la-kuntu khāṭartu bi-nafsī wa-bāraztu ʿasharata ālāfi fārisin wa-qataltu muqaddamahumu al-wazīra Dandāna wa-ẓafirtu bi-fārisi sahmi Sharkāna
sentences.l: So she said to him: By the right of your religion, were it not that I feared that my report would spread, that I am of the daughters of Rūm, I would have hazarded with my self, and duelled ten thousand horsemen, and killed their foremost one the vizier Dandān, and got-the-better of the horseman of the lot-of Sharkān.
sentences.i: Then she said to him: "By the right of your religion, were I not afraid that the news would spread that I am one of the daughters of Rūm, I would have risked my life and fought ten thousand horsemen, killed their commander the vizier Dandān, and taken Sharkān's own champion."
sentences.n: وَحَقِّ دِينِكَ is an oath: the وَ swears, and the genitive follows. خَاطَرَ بِنَفْسِهِ is "to risk oneself", بِـ marking what is staked. ظَفِرَ بِـ is "to get the better of, to win". The last phrase, بِفَارِسِ سَهْمِ شَرْكَانَ, is obscure: سَهْم is "arrow" but also "lot, portion", and Lane gives it, in its sense of share, for a company or division of men. We read "the horseman of Sharkān's division" and render it "Sharkān's own champion" in the free line, but the words may be corrupt for something like "a horseman of Sharkān's arrow-men". Read it as uncertain. The edition prints يشيع خبري اني, "that my report spread, that I am", in two clauses back to back.

sentences.t: وَمَاكَانَ عَلَيَّ فِي ذَلِكَ عَارٌ وَلَٰكِنَّنِي قَرَأْتُ الْكُتُبَ وَتَعَلَّمْتُ الْأَدَبَ مِنْ كَلَامِ الْعَرَبِ
sentences.tr: wa-mākāna ʿalayya fī dhālika ʿārun wa-lākinnanī qaraʾtu al-kutuba wa-taʿallamtu al-adaba min kalāmi al-ʿarab
sentences.l: And there would have been upon me in that no shame; but I have read the books, and learned the courtesy from the speech of the Arabs.
sentences.i: There would have been no shame to me in that; but I have read the books and learned good breeding from the speech of the Arabs.
sentences.n: The edition runs وماكان together, wa-mā kāna, "and there was not"; the shadda on عَلَيَّ is the print's own. In the girl's mouth "upon me … shame" means no disgrace would have fallen on her. الْأَدَب is both "good manners" and "literary learning", the two being one thing for the educated; "the courtesy" keeps both. The print has قرأت with a precomposed hamza, kept. The edition prints ولكنني without the alif of لَٰكِنَّ; it is pointed with a dagger alif.

sentences.t: وَلَسْتُ أَصِفُ لَكَ نَفْسِي بِا لشَّجَاعَةِ مَعَ أَنَّكَ رَأَيْتَ مِنِّي الْعَلَامَةَ وَالصِّنَاعَةَ وَالْقُوَّةَ فِى الصِّرَاعِ وَالْبَرَاعَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-lastu aṣifu laka nafsī bi-al-shajāʿati maʿa annaka raʾayta minnī al-ʿalāmata wa-al-ṣināʿata wa-al-quwwata fī al-ṣirāʿi wa-al-barāʿa
sentences.l: And I am not describing to you myself with the courage, together with that you have seen from me the sign and the craft and the strength in the wrestling, and the excellence.
sentences.i: I do not describe myself to you as brave, although you have seen in me the proofs of skill, the craft, the strength in wrestling, and the mastery.
sentences.n: The edition splits بالشجاعة into با لشجاعة; it is kept, pointed بِا لشَّجَاعَةِ, to be read bi-al-shajāʿa. وَلَسْتُ أَصِفُ is "I am not describing", لَسْتُ taking a present verb as its predicate; وَصَفَ لَكَ نَفْسِي is "to describe oneself to you", بِـ introducing the quality. الْعَلَامَة is "sign, token" (of her ability); the pointing الْعَلَّامَة, "the great scholar", would also fit the letters but suits the list of skills less well.

sentences.t: وَلَوْ حَضَرَ شَرْكَانُ مَكَانَكَ فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَقِيلَ لَهُ نُطَّ هَذَا النَّهْرَ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-law ḥaḍara Sharkānu makānaka fī hādhihi al-laylati wa-qīla lahu nuṭṭa hādhā al-nahra lam yaqdir ʿalā dhālika
sentences.l: And if Sharkān were present in your place on this night, and it were said to him "Leap this river," he would not be able to do that.
sentences.i: And if Sharkān stood where you stand tonight, and were told, "Leap this river," he could not do it.
sentences.n: نُطَّ is the command "leap!"; the shadda on ط is the print's own. هَذَا النَّهْرَ is its object, "leap (over) this river". مَكَانَكَ is "in your place", the accusative of place.

sentences.t: وَإِنِّي أَوَدُّوَأَنْ الْمَسِيحُ يَرْمِيَهُ بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ فِي هَذَا الدَّيْرِ حَتَّى أَخْرُجَ لَهُ فِي صِفَةِ الرِّجَالِ وَأٓسِرَهُ وَأَجْعَلَهُ فِى الْأَغْلَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-innī awaddu wa-an al-Masīḥu yarmiyahu bayna yadayya fī hādhā al-dayri ḥattā akhruja lahu fī ṣifati al-rijāli wa-āsirahu wa-ajʿalahu fī al-aghlāl
sentences.l: And I, I wish — and that the Messiah cast him between my two hands in this monastery, until I go out to him in the likeness of the men, and take-him-captive, and put him in the fetters.
sentences.i: And I wish that the Messiah might cast him into my hands here in this monastery, so that I might go out to him in the dress of men, and take him prisoner, and put him in chains.
sentences.n: The edition prints اودّوان as one word, with the shadda on the د: it reads أَوَدُّ وَأَنْ, "I wish, and that". The extra "and" is hard to explain, perhaps a slip; we point it so the letters stand and give أَنْ the subjunctive يَرْمِيَهُ. المسيح is Christ, to whom the Byzantine girl prays. بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ, "between my two hands", is "into my power". فِي صِفَةِ الرِّجَالِ is "in the guise of men". In وَأٓسِرَهُ the print has a single alif for what should be the first-person أَأْسِرَ, so we put a maddah on it: read wa-āsirahu, "and take him captive". The edition prints فى for في.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُ—بَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahra Zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿan al-kalāmi al-m—bāḥ
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the speech the permitted.
sentences.i: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent and said no more of the permitted words.
sentences.n: This is the usual closing formula of a night. The last word is damaged in the source text (الم—باح, with a dash where letters are lost); we keep it exactly, and point around the gap الْمُ—بَاحِ. Almost certainly it is الْمُبَاح, "the permitted", the usual end of this formula, "she fell silent from the permitted speech". شَهْرَ زَادَ is printed as two words.
